claims.statement: The requested decision is endorsement of the approved architecture and coding baseline plus a controlled roadmap; it is not deployment approval.
claims.caveat: Phase 6 remains subject to independent review and human approval.

claims.statement: Release 1 has an approved evidence chain from requirements through a locally implemented and statically validated package.
claims.caveat: The evidence chain does not establish deployed or runtime behaviour.

claims.statement: Azure sign-in, target validation, what-if, deployment, cloud validation, runtime testing and operating-effectiveness evidence do not exist.
claims.caveat: No inference about target behaviour is permitted.

claims.statement: The approved business target is to reduce median due diligence from 12 weeks to no more than 3 weeks within 12 months of programme approval.
claims.caveat: This is a target, not an achieved benefit.

claims.statement: Release 1 is limited to the first 20 eligible new private-equity opportunities with recorded deal and jurisdiction eligibility.
claims.caveat: Eligibility definitions remain owner-bound under VAL-003.

claims.statement: Deal professionals validate material outputs, Legal and Compliance review specialist conclusions, Internal Audit owns the independent verdict, and the Investment Committee retains every investment decision.
claims.caveat: No automated decision authority is authorised.

claims.statement: The approved solution scope supports governed evidence ingestion, extraction, comparison, anomaly and risk analysis, citation, review and draft recommendation preparation.
claims.caveat: All functions remain assistive and subject to human controls.

claims.statement: The value logic is evidence-to-draft cycle-time improvement through governed reuse, grounded analysis and explicit human review.
claims.caveat: Chief Investment Officer must validate benefit measures against dated operational evidence.

claims.statement: Quality and control outcomes are defined as acceptance thresholds, including citation, extraction, prohibited-action prevention and auditable review.
claims.caveat: Threshold performance has not been established in a cloud runtime.

claims.statement: The chosen approach is a case-centred, evidence-enveloped, assistive workflow with common fail-closed policy and separated decision authority.

sources.section: Candidate architecture decisions AD-001, AD-003, AD-004, AD-005

claims.caveat: Implementation does not prove runtime effectiveness.

claims.statement: Rejected alternatives include autonomous decisioning, source write-back, UI-only controls, shared environments and post-ingestion licence review.

sources.section: Candidate architecture decisions AD-002, AD-004, AD-005, AD-006, AD-010

claims.caveat: Alternatives are rejected for this approved baseline, not universally.

claims.statement: The principal trade-off is stronger evidence, isolation and human control in exchange for more gates, identities, operational complexity and release latency.
claims.caveat: Cost impact is not quantified.

claims.statement: The approved vendor-neutral target contains 19 Architecture Building Blocks and 10 architecture decisions.
claims.caveat: Counts describe the approved logical architecture, not deployed services.

claims.statement: The target flow preserves source authority, quarantines and admits evidence, grounds analysis, enforces review, and records only a draft recommendation before committee decision.
claims.caveat: The diagram is logical and vendor-neutral.

claims.statement: Independent validation evidence is isolated so delivery and operations cannot issue or modify the Internal Audit verdict.
claims.caveat: Verdict issuance remains one of three authority conflicts in the implemented package.

claims.statement: The approved Azure design is a private AI-focused landing zone with separated platform, non-production, production and Internal Audit assurance boundaries.

sources.section: Executive summary; Citadel architecture and landing-zone topology

claims.caveat: Exact tenant, subscriptions, regions and network values remain fail-closed owner inputs.

claims.statement: The design uses private ingress and APIs, internal Container Apps, Azure SQL Database, Blob Storage, Azure AI Search, regional Azure OpenAI and Document Intelligence.
claims.caveat: Service selection is design intent; target availability and compatibility are unvalidated.

claims.statement: Well-Architected balance favours private security, zonal primary plus warm recovery, evidence-led sizing, separated workloads and explicit operational gates.
claims.caveat: Two-region operation and recovery behaviour are untested.

claims.statement: The approved implementation sequence contains 17 deployable units, five work packages and 46 acyclic dependencies.
claims.caveat: The sequence is an approved plan, not an executed deployment.

claims.statement: The Phase 5 release manifest binds 116 deployable source files and all 17 implementation units.
claims.caveat: Deployable source does not mean deployment-ready.

claims.statement: The retained local validation run passed ten steps; assurance reports also record 55 of 55 IaC tests and 77 of 77 application tests passing.
claims.caveat: These are local/static results, not target or runtime tests.

claims.statement: Source and container evidence reports zero HIGH or CRITICAL findings and zero detected secrets in the retained scans.
claims.caveat: Scan results are point-in-time local evidence and not a security certification.

claims.statement: No approved numeric business case, ROI, cost total, Azure price, rate or realised benefit exists.
claims.caveat: Do not infer financial values from architecture or validation evidence.

claims.statement: An owner-approved Azure Pricing Calculator estimate requires exact regions, capacity, usage, resilience and commercial inputs.
claims.caveat: Owners: FinOps, Enterprise Platform and Chief Investment Officer; source must be dated.

claims.statement: Benefit validation requires dated baseline and post-adoption cycle-time, quality, review-effort and exception evidence.
claims.caveat: Chief Investment Officer and control owners must approve measures and dated sources.

claims.statement: Exactly three authority conflicts remain open: assurance verdict issuance, analysis execution and audit evidence export.
claims.caveat: All three remain fail closed and unwaived.

claims.statement: Exactly fourteen owner-bound controls remain open, comprising VAL-001 to VAL-005, AFFB-RES-001 to AFFB-RES-002 and CC1-OWN-001 to CC1-OWN-007.
claims.caveat: Named-owner evidence is required before each stated boundary.

claims.statement: Exactly two retained AFF-B minor gaps remain open: AFFB-CC001-R2-MIN-001 and AFFB-CC001-R3-MIN-002.
claims.caveat: Neither gap is waived or closed.

claims.statement: DORA applicability, AI Act classification, official legal mappings, production values, retention finalisation and target behaviour remain owner or future-authorisation matters.
claims.caveat: No legal conclusion, compliance certification or operating-effectiveness claim is made.

claims.statement: The recommended board action is to endorse the approved baseline and controlled roadmap while keeping deployment outside this decision.
claims.caveat: Endorsement does not approve Phase 6, deployment or runtime testing.

claims.statement: The controlled next step is owner evidence closure and separately authorised target validation planning before any optional deployment decision.
claims.caveat: Phase 7 remains separately human-invocable and unauthorised.

claims.statement: Phase 8 runtime testing remains optional, separate and unauthorised; it requires a successful approved Phase 7 deployment and a separate human invocation.
claims.caveat: No optional phase is invoked by this recommendation.
